diagram-sitplan-consistency.message: Placement lacks valid circuit point identifier
diagram-sitplan-consistency.details: Every sitplan placement of an outlet/light/control unit must have an endpoint that belongs to a circuit with a branch label (circuit letter + number). Switches must reference controlled loads.
diagram-sitplan-consistency.remediation: Ensure all placements are associated with endpoints that have valid circuit identifiers (e.g., "A1", "B3").

hidden-situation-plan-symbols.message: Devices are hidden on the situation plan
hidden-situation-plan-symbols.details: Hidden devices are omitted from the situation plan.
hidden-situation-plan-symbols.remediation: Open Show hidden and choose which devices to show.

unplaced-situation-plan-symbols.shortTitle: Devices not placed on the situation plan
unplaced-situation-plan-symbols.message: Devices are not placed on the situation plan yet
unplaced-situation-plan-symbols.details: Devices that are not placed yet are missing from the situation plan.
unplaced-situation-plan-symbols.remediation: Place them on the plan, for example with the Quick Placer.

sources-consistency.message: Main supply origin should be specified
sources-consistency.details: If main supply has origin other than grid (e.g., pv_inverter), it must be represented consistently in the installation.
sources-consistency.remediation: Specify the main supply origin in the installation settings.

nonhousehold-board-grounded-network.message: Board does not show its grounded network system
nonhousehold-board-grounded-network.details: A non-domestic board marking must identify its grounded network system.
nonhousehold-board-grounded-network.remediation: Open the board properties, enable Net type on diagram, and select the applicable TT, TN, or IT earthing system.

nonhousehold-board-numbering.message: Board sequence numbering is not shown
nonhousehold-board-numbering.details: Each non-domestic board must carry an individual sequence number.
nonhousehold-board-numbering.remediation: Open the board properties and enable Panel numbering.

nonhousehold-circuit-cable-length.message: Circuit cable length is not shown
nonhousehold-circuit-cable-length.details: Non-domestic circuit documentation must include the length of electrical lines.
nonhousehold-circuit-cable-length.remediation: Select the circuit wire, enter a positive length, and enable Show wire length on one-wire.

household-breaking-capacity.message: Breaker breaking capacity is below 3000 A
household-breaking-capacity.details: In household installations, overcurrent devices after the connection device need a breaking capacity of at least 3000 A.
household-breaking-capacity.remediation: Select the breaker and choose a breaking capacity of 3000 A or more.

household-supply-breaking-capacity.message: Supply breaker breaking capacity is too low
household-supply-breaking-capacity.details: The connection device before the meter needs at least 6000 A. Breakers after the meter need at least 3000 A.
household-supply-breaking-capacity.remediation: Select the supply breaker and raise its breaking capacity.

maximum-protected-length.message: Circuit cable exceeds the maximum protected length
maximum-protected-length.details: A short circuit at the far end must still trip the breaker instantly.
maximum-protected-length.remediation: Use a larger cable section, a shorter route, or a lower rating or curve.

overcurrent-upstream.details: Every circuit must have an overcurrent protective device (MCB, RCBO, or fuse) upstream.
overcurrent-upstream.remediation: Add an MCB, RCBO, or fuse upstream of the circuit to provide overcurrent protection.

rcd-grouping.message: Too many circuits under one 30 mA RCD
rcd-grouping.details: A 30 mA RCD should protect at most 8 circuits (RCBO-protected circuits are excluded from this count) to reduce nuisance tripping and limit leakage current accumulation.
rcd-grouping.remediation: Reduce the number of circuits under this RCD or split into multiple RCDs. Circuits protected by an RCBO do not count toward the limit.

rcd-selectivity.message: RCD selectivity: upstream must be less sensitive than downstream
rcd-selectivity.details: The main RCD (e.g. 300 mA for fire protection) must be upstream of more sensitive RCDs (e.g. 30 mA for personal protection). Never place a 30 mA RCD upstream of a 300 mA device.
rcd-selectivity.remediation: Ensure the main supply RCD is 300 mA (or less sensitive) and panel RCDs are 30 mA (more sensitive), so that upstream sensitivity (mA) is greater than downstream.

bathroom-rcd-30ma.message: Bathroom/wet room circuit requires 30 mA RCD/RCBO protection
bathroom-rcd-30ma.details: Circuits supplying rooms with a bath and/or shower must be protected by a high/very high sensitivity residual current device (typically 30 mA). Because room detection is ambiguous, this check triggers when the circuit notes mention bathroom/bath/shower terms in any language.
bathroom-rcd-30ma.remediation: Route this circuit through a 30 mA RCD, or protect it with a 30 mA RCBO. If the circuit does not actually supply a bathroom/wet room, adjust the circuit notes.

max-endpoints-per-circuit.details: Each circuit should have a maximum number of endpoints to ensure proper load distribution and protection.
max-endpoints-per-circuit.remediation: Split the circuit into multiple circuits to reduce the endpoint count.

minimum-lighting-circuits.message: At least two separate lighting circuits required
minimum-lighting-circuits.details: For a typical dwelling, AREI requires at least two separate circuits for lighting (lighting or mixed leaf circuits). Container circuits with sub-circuits are not counted.
minimum-lighting-circuits.remediation: Add a second lighting or mixed circuit so lighting is spread across at least two circuits.

installation-earthing.details: No earth electrode is shown on any board. This can be valid, but most installations need one earthing point.
installation-earthing.remediation: Add earthing on the main board, or drop it on a secondary board if the electrode is there.

multiple-earthing-locations.shortTitle: Earthing on more than one board
multiple-earthing-locations.message: Earthing is shown on more than one board
multiple-earthing-locations.details: The installation has earth electrodes on separate boards. Confirm this is intended; typically there is a single earthing point.
multiple-earthing-locations.remediation: Keep earthing on one board and remove the extra earth stem.

cable-cross-section.message: Circuit has cable segments without cross-section
cable-cross-section.details: All cable segments must have a valid cross-section specified.
cable-cross-section.remediation: Specify the cross-section (sectionMm2) for all cable segments in the circuit.

breaker-vs-cross-section.details: The MCB/RCBO rating must not exceed the admissible current for the cable cross-section.
breaker-vs-cross-section.remediation: Reduce the breaker rating or increase the cable cross-section to meet AREI limits.

minimum-cross-section.message: Cable cross-section too small for circuit type
minimum-cross-section.details: Each circuit type has a minimum required cable cross-section according to AREI 5.2.1.
minimum-cross-section.remediation: Increase the cable cross-section to at least the minimum value for this circuit type.

cascade-protection.message: Downstream breaker rated higher than upstream breaker
cascade-protection.details: Downstream circuit breakers should not be rated higher than their upstream protection.
cascade-protection.remediation: Adjust breaker ratings so that downstream devices are rated equal to or below their upstream breaker.

main-rcd.message: Main RCD/RCBO on supply trunk must be present and correctly sized
main-rcd.details: AREI Book 1 requires a main residual current device at the origin of the installation, typically 300 mA type A with at least 40 A rated current.
main-rcd.remediation: Add a main RCD or RCBO on the supply trunk upstream of the main panel and ensure it is at least 40 A, at most 300 mA and at least type A.

board-global-isolation.message: Board lacks a device that disconnects all active conductors
board-global-isolation.details: Each distribution board, including sub-boards, must be disconnectable from all active conductors either by a local disconnector in the board or by an upstream feeder device.
board-global-isolation.remediation: Add a local main switch/disconnector in the board, or ensure an upstream feeder protection/disconnector can disconnect all active conductors of this board.

board-local-isolation-hint.message: Board is only isolatable via upstream device
board-local-isolation-hint.details: This board can be disconnected upstream, but has no local disconnector in the board itself. Inspectors commonly expect local disconnectability for safety and usability.
board-local-isolation-hint.remediation: Consider adding a local main switch/disconnector in this board.

switch-load-reference.details: Every switch must have at least one controlled load (controlledEndpointIds) or explicit "controls" reference.
switch-load-reference.remediation: Add controlledEndpointIds to the switch to specify which loads it controls.

switch-sequence.message: Two-way and cross switches are not in a valid order on this branch
switch-sequence.details: Staircase switching needs exactly two two-way switches: either two-way → two-way, or two-way → (any crosses) → two-way. No extra two-ways and no chaining beyond that pattern.
switch-sequence.remediation: Use exactly two two-ways: two-way → two-way, or two-way → cross → … → cross → two-way. Remove any third two-way or two-way placed between crosses.

electrical-domain.details: A wire's domain must match the expected input domain of the connected component. Only conversion components may connect different domains.
electrical-domain.remediation: Set the wire domain to match the component's input/output, or use a conversion component (transformer, rectifier, inverter, DC-DC) where domain changes.

dc-cross-section-heuristic.message: Estimated DC current may be high for wire section
dc-cross-section-heuristic.details: This warning uses a conservative estimate on DC segments (I ~= P/U) based on known converter/device power and DC voltage values. It is informational and should be confirmed against real device specs and installation conditions.
dc-cross-section-heuristic.remediation: Check converter output power and actual DC voltage/current. If needed, increase DC wire section, reduce expected load, or adjust converter/device configuration.

post-main-bus-pe-conductor.shortTitle: Missing PE path after main bus
post-main-bus-pe-conductor.message: AC circuits after the main bus need a continuous protective-earth path
post-main-bus-pe-conductor.details: Protective earth may be included in the cable (G) or installed as an independent conductor alongside the active conductors. Internal links between protection devices may carry only active conductors; PE remains continuous through the panel earth bar and must not pass through those devices. DC wiring is not checked.
post-main-bus-pe-conductor.remediation: Provide a continuous PE path with outgoing AC wiring. Use a G cable or a correctly sized and installed independent PE conductor.

heavy-appliance-dedicated-circuit.shortTitle: Heavy appliance not on own circuit
heavy-appliance-dedicated-circuit.message: Heavy fixed appliances must be on their own dedicated circuit
heavy-appliance-dedicated-circuit.details: Electric cookers, hobs, ovens, washing machines, tumble dryers and dishwashers each require a dedicated circuit without additional sockets, lighting or other loads.
heavy-appliance-dedicated-circuit.remediation: Move each heavy fixed appliance to its own circuit, or split the existing circuit so that each such appliance has its own overcurrent protection and cable.

fixed-appliance-dedicated-hint.message: Fixed appliance shares a circuit that is not dedicated
fixed-appliance-dedicated-hint.details: Fixed appliances are often placed on their own circuit so the cable size and protection match the appliance and possible future replacements.
fixed-appliance-dedicated-hint.remediation: Consider moving the fixed appliance to its own circuit without extra sockets, lights or other loads.

stove-sizing-hint.details: Typical Belgian practice is to feed full-size electric cookers with a dedicated circuit around 32A and 6mm² copper, even if smaller values may be legally acceptable when matched to the appliance rating.
stove-sizing-hint.remediation: Consider increasing the cooker circuit breaker rating and cable cross-section to around 32A and 6mm², or verify that the current design matches the actual stove rating.

rcd-required-by-circuit-type.message: 30 mA RCD required for designated household and EV circuits
rcd-required-by-circuit-type.details: Lighting, general-purpose sockets, washing machines, tumble dryers, dishwashers and EV charging circuits require 30 mA residual-current protection under AREI 4.2.4.3(b) and 7.22.4.1.
rcd-required-by-circuit-type.remediation: Route these circuits through an RCD or RCBO with 30 mA sensitivity, either at the panel or via a main 30 mA device.

eendraad-orphans.message: Circuit, endpoint or frame is inconsistent with the one-line diagram
eendraad-orphans.details: Some circuits, endpoints or frame contents are not correctly linked, so they do not appear in the one-line (eendraad) view or appear under the wrong protection. Endpoints that should appear on the floor plan may also lack any sitplan placement. Fix circuit subcircuit assignments, branch endpoint lists, frame content references, or add plan placements.
eendraad-orphans.remediation: Ensure each circuit is under only one protection; add every endpoint to a branch (or remove it); fix or remove frame content references to missing items; add a floor-plan placement for endpoints that are missing from the plan.

duplicate-panel-protection-label.message: Two or more protections on this panel share the same label
duplicate-panel-protection-label.details: Each protection on one panel (main bus, secondary bus, supply strip, or incoming feed) must have a unique label so circuits stay identifiable on the one-line diagram and panel layout. This is not a wiring orphan — it is a naming conflict.
duplicate-panel-protection-label.remediation: Rename one of the conflicting protections, or turn on automatic naming so letters are reassigned without duplicates.

control-link-integrity.message: A control link or domotica address needs attention
control-link-integrity.details: A contact points to a device that no longer exists, two connections use the same channel on one device, or an address does not fit the device system.
control-link-integrity.remediation: Choose an existing device in Operated by, give each connection its own channel, or correct the address.

converter-backup-labels.message: A protection or endpoint on the backup supply is not labeled
converter-backup-labels.details: Backup-supply items are outside the main bus and are not named automatically.
converter-backup-labels.remediation: Add a clear manual label to every protection and endpoint on the inverter backup branch.

orphanDetection.circuitRefMismatch: Circuit {{circuitCode}} is listed under protection "{{listedUnderLabel}}" but appears in the one-line diagram under circuit {{parentCircuitCode}} (protection "{{displayedUnderLabel}}").
orphanDetection.protectionReferenceConflict: Circuit {{circuitCode}} is referenced by multiple protections ({{protectionLabels}}). RCD/RCBO nesting must keep the child under its MCB and link it from the anchor circuit. Repair the one-line topology before continuing.
orphanDetection.endpointNotInBranch: Endpoint "{{endpointLabel}}" on circuit {{circuitCode}} is not on any branch and will not appear on the one-line diagram.
orphanDetection.branchRefsMissingEndpoint: Branch "{{branchLabel}}" on circuit {{circuitCode}} references missing endpoint {{endpointId}}.
orphanDetection.frameContentOrphans: Frame "{{frameTitle}}" references missing or invalid content ({{contentId}}).
orphanDetection.subCircuitSelfReference: Circuit "{{circuitCode}}" lists its own id in subCircuitIds (invalid). It may not render on the one-line diagram but still appear in circuit pickers.
orphanDetection.endpointOnPanelCircuit: Endpoint "{{endpointLabel}}" is attached to the PANEL pseudo-circuit and will not appear correctly on the one-line diagram.
orphanDetection.endpointMultipleFloorPlacements: Endpoint "{{endpointLabel}}" is placed on {{floorCount}} floors, but this symbol should have only one placement.
orphanDetection.planPlacementIdentityConflict: Situation-plan placement "{{placementId}}" is shared by {{ownerLabels}}. Symbols may overlap, disappear, or select together; recreate the affected duplicates with unique placements.
orphanDetection.panelDistributionLabelDrift: Panel symbol "{{endpointLabel}}" does not match board "{{panelName}}" (circuit {{circuitCode}}).
orphanDetection.panelMissingOneWireSymbol: Panel "{{panelName}}" exists but has no one-wire feeder symbol/link.
orphanDetection.panelGridDuplicateModule: Panel canvas shows "{{moduleLabel}}" more than once; keep the fuller module and hide the weaker duplicate.
orphanDetection.supplyTrunkMisplacedInMainGrid: Supply device "{{label}}" is placed on the main panel grid (row {{row}}, column {{col}}) but must live in the supply strip only — panel canvas and one-line supply chain disagree.
orphanDetection.supplyTrunkVisualPlacementMissing: Supply device "{{label}}" exists in the supply topology but has no reachable panel-canvas placement.
orphanDetection.splitBusWithoutBackupSupply: Panel "{{panelName}}" has {{busSectionCount}} bus sections but no connected backup supply. Merge it back onto one grid feed.
orphanDetection.branchMultiplierEndpointsSplit: Circuit {{circuitCode}}: branch "{{branchLabel}}" lists {{absorbCount}} extra multiplier symbol(s) (e.g. lights) as separate endpoints; they should be one endpoint with multiple plan placements. Use Repair in the Orphan Inspector.

supplyModePaths.details: The one-line topology does not provide a complete, coordinated grid and backup path for {{phases}}.
supplyModePaths.remediation: Reconnect the grid, backup and load sides so every shown phase has a complete supply path.

supplyConductorProtectionCoordination.message: {{protectionLabel}}: {{section}} mm² conductor is too small for {{ratingA}} A protection
supplyConductorProtectionCoordination.details: The drawn {{section}} mm² supply conductor may be protected at no more than {{maxRatingA}} A by this protective device, but the shown rating is {{ratingA}} A.
supplyConductorProtectionCoordination.remediation: Increase the conductor cross-section or reduce the upstream protective-device rating.

duplicatePanelProtectionLabels.message: Protection label "{{label}}" is used {{count}} times on this panel
duplicatePanelProtectionLabels.details: Duplicate protection names on the same panel (main bus, secondary bus, or supply) make circuits hard to identify. Rename one protection or enable automatic naming.

dangling.message: {{endpoint}} is operated by a device that no longer exists
dangling.details: Pick another device in Operated by, or clear the link.

duplicateChannel.details: Each input or output channel of a device can be used once. Give each connection its own channel.

invalidAddress.message: {{endpoint}} on {{device}}: address {{address}} does not fit this system
invalidAddress.details: Enter the address in the notation of the selected domotica system, or change the system.

protection.details: Protections on an inverter backup-supply branch are not named automatically. Add a clear manual label.

endpoint.details: Endpoints on an inverter backup-supply branch are not named automatically. Add a clear manual label.

group.message: {{count}} protections may not match this {{availablePoleCount}}-pole supply
group.details: Affected protections: {{deviceLabels}}. Check their phase and pole settings at this supply transition.

neutralUnavailable.message: {{deviceLabel}} uses neutral, but this network has none
neutralUnavailable.details: This combination may not make sense. Check the phase or pole setting.

tooManyPoles.message: {{deviceLabel}} is {{poleCount}}-pole; that may be too many for this {{availablePoleCount}}-pole supply
tooManyPoles.details: This combination may not make sense. Check the pole setting.

tooFewPoles.message: {{deviceLabel}} is {{poleCount}}-pole; that may be too few for this three-phase network
tooFewPoles.details: This combination may not make sense. Check the pole setting.

hasUpstreamOvercurrent.details: Every circuit must have an upstream overcurrent protective device (MCB, RCBO, or fuse).

countUnderThreshold.details: The count of {{count}} exceeds the maximum allowed threshold of {{threshold}}.

hasValue.details: The required field {{fieldName}} is missing or undefined.

switchHasControlledLoads.details: Every switch must control at least one load (light, outlet, or appliance).

wrongTwoWayCount.message: Branch {{branchLabel}} on circuit {{circuitCode}}: needs exactly two two-way switches
wrongTwoWayCount.details: This branch has one or more than two two-way switches in the staircase chain. Use exactly two: two-way → two-way, or two-way → crosses → two-way.

twoWayChaining.message: Branch {{branchLabel}} on circuit {{circuitCode}}: extra two-way in the chain
twoWayChaining.details: Do not place a two-way between crosses or after the pattern. Valid order is two-way → (crosses only) → two-way.

crossWithoutLeadingTwoWay.message: Branch {{branchLabel}} on circuit {{circuitCode}}: cross switch needs a two-way before it
crossWithoutLeadingTwoWay.details: Start with a two-way switch, then any cross switches, then the second two-way.

crossWithoutTrailingTwoWay.message: Branch {{branchLabel}} on circuit {{circuitCode}}: cross switch needs a two-way after it
crossWithoutTrailingTwoWay.details: End the chain with a two-way switch after the cross switches, before the load.

placementHasValidIdentifier.message: Placement for "{{endpointLabel}}" lacks valid circuit point identifier
placementHasValidIdentifier.details: The sitplan placement for "{{endpointLabel}}" must be linked to an endpoint that has a valid circuit letter and point number (e.g. "A1"). Check that this symbol is on a circuit on the one-line diagram.

hiddenSituationPlanSymbolsAreVisible.message_one: {{count}} device is hidden on the situation plan
hiddenSituationPlanSymbolsAreVisible.message_other: {{count}} devices are hidden on the situation plan
hiddenSituationPlanSymbolsAreVisible.message_few: {{count}} devices are hidden on the situation plan
hiddenSituationPlanSymbolsAreVisible.message_many: {{count}} devices are hidden on the situation plan

situationPlanSymbolsArePlaced.message_other: {{count}} devices are not placed on the situation plan yet
situationPlanSymbolsArePlaced.message_few: {{count}} devices are not placed on the situation plan yet
situationPlanSymbolsArePlaced.message_many: {{count}} devices are not placed on the situation plan yet

cableHasCrossSection.message: Circuit has cable segments without cross-section
cableHasCrossSection.details: All cable segments must have a valid cross-section specified.

breakerSizeMatchesCrossSection.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}}: breaker rating {{breakerRating}}A exceeds maximum {{maxRating}}A for {{section}}mm² cable
breakerSizeMatchesCrossSection.details: For circuit {{circuitCode}}, the breaker rating {{breakerRating}}A is higher than the admissible current for a {{section}}mm² copper cable (maximum {{maxRating}}A). Reduce the breaker rating or increase the cable size.

minimumCrossSection.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}}: cable cross-section {{section}}mm² is below minimum {{required}}mm²
minimumCrossSection.details: Circuit {{circuitCode}} uses a {{section}}mm² cable, but the AREI minimum for this circuit type is {{required}}mm².

dcCrossSectionHeuristic.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}}: DC sizing warning — estimated {{estimatedCurrentA}}A exceeds ~{{sectionAmpacity}}A for {{section}}mm²
dcCrossSectionHeuristic.details: Heuristic calculation on the DC section of circuit {{circuitCode}}: I ≈ P/U = {{estimatedPowerW}}W / {{estimatedVoltage}}V = {{estimatedCurrentA}}A. The weakest DC wire section is {{section}}mm² (simplified reference ~{{sectionAmpacity}}A). Voltage source: {{voltageSourceLabel}}. This is a warning, not a hard AREI error; verify the converter and device specifications.

cascadeProtectionRatings.message: Downstream protection rating exceeds upstream breaker rating
cascadeProtectionRatings.details: A downstream MCB/RCBO on a circuit must not be rated higher than its upstream protection.

supplyHasMainBreaker.message: Main supply has no upstream breaker or main switch
supplyHasMainBreaker.details: The supply trunk should include a main breaker or main switch upstream of the main panel.

hasSupplyOrigin.message: Main supply origin should be specified
hasSupplyOrigin.details: The main supply origin (grid, generator, pv_inverter, etc.) should be specified in the installation settings.

installationHasEarthing.details: No earth electrode is shown on any board. This can be valid, but most installations need one earthing point.

installationHasSingleEarthingLocation.message: Earthing is shown on more than one board
installationHasSingleEarthingLocation.details: The installation has earth electrodes on separate boards. Confirm this is intended; typically there is a single earthing point.

nonHouseholdPanelShowsGroundedNetwork.message: Board {{panelName}} does not show its grounded network system
nonHouseholdPanelShowsGroundedNetwork.details: Non-domestic boards must identify their grounded network system. Enable the net-type label and select the applicable TT, TN, or IT system in the board properties.

nonHouseholdPanelNumberingIsShown.details: Non-domestic boards must carry an individual sequence number. Enable panel numbering in the board properties.

nonHouseholdCircuitShowsCableLength.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}} does not show a cable length
nonHouseholdCircuitShowsCableLength.details: Non-domestic circuit diagrams must include electrical-line lengths. Enter a positive wire length and enable its visibility on the one-wire diagram.

householdBoardBreakingCapacity.details: In household installations, overcurrent devices after the connection device need a breaking capacity of at least 3000 A.

householdSupplyBreakingCapacity.details: The connection device before the meter needs at least 6000 A. Overcurrent devices after it need at least 3000 A.

circuitWithinMaximumProtectedLength.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}}: {{lengthM}} m of cable exceeds the protected length of {{maxLengthM}} m
circuitWithinMaximumProtectedLength.details: A short circuit at the far end must still trip the {{curve}}{{ratingA}} instantly ({{tripCurrentA}} A). With {{sectionMm2}} mm² that allows at most {{maxLengthM}} m. Use a larger section, a shorter route, or a lower rating or curve.

rcdHasTooManyCircuits.details: Circuits under one 30 mA RCD should respect a maximum count ({{threshold}}) to reduce nuisance tripping and limit leakage current accumulation. RCBO-protected circuits are excluded.

rcdSelectivity.message: RCD selectivity: upstream RCD must be less sensitive than downstream (e.g. 300 mA main, 30 mA sub)
rcdSelectivity.details: The main RCD (e.g. 300 mA for fire protection) must be upstream of more sensitive RCDs (e.g. 30 mA for personal protection). Never place a 30 mA RCD upstream of a 300 mA device.

wetRoomRequires30mAFromCircuitNotes.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}} appears to feed a bathroom (notes), but has no 30 mA RCD/RCBO protection
wetRoomRequires30mAFromCircuitNotes.details: This rule was triggered because the circuit notes contain bathroom/bath/shower keywords (match: {{matched}}). AREI requires circuits supplying rooms with a bath and/or shower to be protected by high/very high sensitivity residual current protection (typically 30 mA). Add an upstream 30 mA RCD or use an RCBO with 30 mA sensitivity for this circuit.

circuitHasTooManyEndpoints.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}} has too many socket-equivalent points ({{endpointCount}} > {{threshold}})
circuitHasTooManyEndpoints.details: Socket and mixed circuit {{circuitCode}} has {{endpointCount}} socket-equivalent points; the maximum is {{threshold}}.

installationHasMinimumLightingCircuits.message: Installation has {{count}} lighting circuit(s); at least {{threshold}} required
installationHasMinimumLightingCircuits.details: AREI 5.3.5.2 requires at least {{threshold}} separate lighting circuits in a typical dwelling. This installation has {{count}} (lighting or mixed leaf circuits).

domainMismatch.message: Cannot connect DC circuit to AC component.
domainMismatch.details: A wire's domain must match the expected input/output domain of the connected component. Only conversion components (transformer, rectifier, inverter, DC-DC) may connect different domains.

missing.message: Main supply has no upstream RCD or RCBO
missing.details: Belgian AREI Book 1 requires a main residual current device at the origin of the installation. Add a main RCD or RCBO on the supply trunk upstream of the main panel.

rating.message: Main RCD/RCBO has rating {{ratingA}}A, below the recommended 40A minimum for residential main devices
rating.details: The main residual current device at the origin of the installation should have a nominal current of at least 40 A. Increase the device rating or adjust the installation design.

sensitivity.message: Main RCD/RCBO sensitivity {{sensitivityMa}} mA exceeds 300 mA maximum
sensitivity.details: The main residual current device at the origin of the installation should have a residual trip current not exceeding 300 mA. Use a 300 mA (or lower) device.

type.message: Main RCD/RCBO must be at least type A, not AC-only
type.details: Under recent AREI revisions, the main residual current device at the origin of the installation must be at least type A (sensitive to pulsating DC). Replace AC-only devices with type A, F or B.

backupSupplyRcdCompliance.message: Backup supply has no equivalent RCD protection
backupSupplyRcdCompliance.details: The backup path needs an RCD or RCBO with a configured sensitivity of at most 300 mA and a nominal current of at least 40 A.
backupSupplyRcdCompliance.remediation: Add a compliant RCD or RCBO on the backup path between the inverter or changeover and the backed-up panel.

panelHasGlobalIsolation.message: Panel {{panelName}} has no device that disconnects all active conductors
panelHasGlobalIsolation.details: Every distribution board must be disconnectable by a scheidingsinrichting that disconnects all active conductors, either locally in the panel or via an upstream feeder device.

panelHasLocalIsolationHint.message: Panel {{panelName}} is disconnectable only upstream, without a local isolator
panelHasLocalIsolationHint.details: The board can be disconnected via an upstream feeder device, but there is no local main switch/disconnector in this panel. Local isolation improves safety and maintainability.

missing.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}} requires RCD/RCBO protection (30 mA), but none was found upstream
missing.details: Lighting, general-purpose socket, washer, dryer, dishwasher and EV charging circuits require 30 mA residual-current protection. Add an RCD or RCBO upstream or route this circuit through an existing 30 mA device.

sensitivity.message: Circuit {{circuitCode}} is protected by RCD(s), but none have 30 mA sensitivity
sensitivity.details: Lighting, general-purpose socket, washer, dryer, dishwasher and EV charging circuits require 30 mA residual-current protection. Adjust the upstream RCD/RCBO sensitivity or route this circuit through a 30 mA device.

dcCompatibility.message: EV circuit {{circuitCode}} has 30 mA RCD protection, but no DC-fault protection was identified
dcCompatibility.details: AREI 7.22.4.1 and 5.3.5.3(f) require the charging point to remain protected against disruptive DC components. Use a Type B RCD, or mark the charger as having coordinated built-in DC residual-current protection/detection (such as 6 mA DC detection).

stoveCircuitSizingHint.message: Cooker circuit {{circuitCode}} uses {{section}}mm² and {{breakerRating}}A; consider at least {{recommendedSection}}mm² and {{recommendedBreaker}}A for a full-size stove
stoveCircuitSizingHint.details: This is a design recommendation: typical Belgian practice is to feed full-size electric cookers with a dedicated circuit of about {{recommendedBreaker}}A and {{recommendedSection}}mm² copper. Smaller values may still be compliant if matched to the actual appliance rating, but can limit future cooker upgrades.

heavyApplianceDedicatedCircuit.message: Heavy fixed appliance(s) {{applianceLabels}} on circuit {{circuitCode}} must be on their own circuit without other loads
heavyApplianceDedicatedCircuit.details: Electric cookers, hobs, ovens, washing machines, tumble dryers and dishwashers each require a dedicated circuit without additional sockets, lighting or other loads.

fixedApplianceDedicatedCircuitHint.message: Fixed appliance(s) {{applianceLabels}} on circuit {{circuitCode}} share the circuit with other loads
fixedApplianceDedicatedCircuitHint.details: Fixed appliances are often placed on their own circuit so the cable size and protection match the appliance and possible future replacements. Consider moving these appliances to their own circuit without extra sockets, lights or other loads.
